extracted.intended_audience: engineers, scientists, and scientifically-literate readers of Popular Science Monthly (late 19th-century)
extracted.subtask_description: Concise engineering/scientific guidance on designing steam-engines to maximize conversion of heat to mechanical power; covers theoretical principles, practical construction, materials, management, and likely directions of improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory unreliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Memory is far more untrustworthy than commonly supposed; only a very small fraction of impressions are retained and can be recalled at will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: treat human testimony with caution; do not assume accurate recall of details even by educated persons. Avoid relying on unaided memory for precise language or order of statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No two reports agree
rubrics_metrics.description: When a short story is repeated down a chain or repeated separately to individuals, no two of the stories agree; all depart more or less from the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental finding (Russian game style): even instant written reports differ. Expect variation even under ideal experimental conditions; use corroboration and contemporaneous records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpolations and omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports commonly contain interpolations and omissions; additions may seriously modify the thought of the original and often are believed by authors to be part of the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that subjects unconsciously substitute subjective material for objective facts. Reporters should not be automatically accused of intentional falsification when differences appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate recording required for accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversation can only be accurately reported when it is taken down at once as the words are uttered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay of minutes to years greatly increases errors; for accurate testimony/transcript, record contemporaneously (e.g., stenographic notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual/eyewitness recall is unreliable
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple persons observe a complex scene (room, furniture, colors, gestures), there will be no agreement in their reports and no report will be accurate even if made at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eyewitness descriptions of scenes should be treated skeptically; corroborating evidence and physical records preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Myth-making from memory distortions
rubrics_metrics.description: A myth can be made in a minute: interpolations/additions to reported conversations quickly create convincing but false narratives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against rapid spread of altered accounts; check original written sources where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory is domain-specific (varieties of memory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Memory is simply a register of a small fraction of impressions; there are as many kinds of memory as there are different faculties—memory measures the talent peculiar to the individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not generalize a person's memory ability across domains; give weight to specialized memory relevant to the matter at hand (e.g., domain experts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert testimony privileged
rubrics_metrics.description: World rests its faith exclusively on the testimony of experts and, for claims of new discoveries, on the testimony of a few of the very highest character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In scientific and novel claims, prioritize testimony from recognized experts (experts of experts) over broad but non-specialist concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing memory by controlled repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Controlled experiments (repeating same story separately and comparing written recollections) show systematic variations according to story complexity and individual memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use controlled experimental protocols to assess reliability of testimony; account for individual differences and story complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design goal of steam-engine
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a machine which shall, in the most perfect manner possible, convert the kinetic energy of heat-motion, as derived from the combustion of fuel, into mechanical power, using steam as the receiver and conveyer of that heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All design choices should be evaluated against this primary functional objective: efficiency of conversion from heat to mechanical power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual assessment: science and engineering
rubrics_metrics.description: Two distinct inquiries must be addressed: (1) What are the scientific principles involved? (2) How shall we construct a machine that efficiently embodies these principles and accords with well-settled engineering practice?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate designs both by theoretical thermodynamic principles and by practical manufacturability, durability, and operational considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize temperature difference
rubrics_metrics.description: Success increases as we work between more widely-separated limits of temperature: higher steam temperature at entry and lower temperature at discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to raise steam admission temperature and lower exhaust temperature; trade-offs must consider material limits and condenser performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize losses by dissipation and friction
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide against losses by dissipation of heat (conduction and radiation) and of power by friction to improve economic efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insulate to reduce conduction/radiation; use good bearing design and lubrication to reduce frictional losses; quantify losses and prioritize remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dry steam to reduce internal condensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain and maintain dry steam (via superheating, steam-jacketing, or both) to check internal condensation and re-evaporation that cause heat loss with great expansion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design boilers/cylinders to supply and preserve dry steam; consider superheaters, jackets, and cylinder linings of low conductivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher pressure and greater expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: A continual increase of steam-pressure and greater expansion has characterized improvement and increases engine duty (efficiency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use safely higher pressures and greater expansion ratios where materials and design permit; accompany with improved workmanship and precautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound/double-cylinder engines reduce losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of compound (double-cylinder) engines reduces friction and saves heat that would otherwise be lost through internal condensation and re-evaporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider multi-stage expansion (compound engines) particularly for marine and high-expansion applications to capture more work from steam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve-gear for high piston speeds: positive motion and governor control
rubrics_metrics.description: At very high piston-speeds the standard 'drop cut-off' detachable valve gear may fail; successful valve-gear must provide positive motion and be easily and sensitively adjusted by the governor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For high-speed engines (e.g., ~1,000 ft/min), adopt positive-motion valve mechanisms, balanced valves, and governors with both sensitivity and power for reliable control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiation of machine functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvement proceeds by differentiation: separating the functions (boiler, cylinder, condenser, pumps) into distinct organs, each simplified and optimized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design modular, specialized components for each function rather than monolithic multipurpose vessels; this enables optimized materials, form, and manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recover rejected heat (binary vapor engine and reworking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain rejected heat within the system and utilize it (e.g., binary vapor-engine which uses condenser heat to evaporate a volatile liquid that produces additional work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate schemes that rework exhaust heat (binary/vapor or regenerative cycles); recognize mechanical difficulties but consider them promising for future efficiency gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiler combustion and heat absorption
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve boilers by more complete combustion without excess air and by more thorough absorption of heat from furnace gases; mechanical draught may be preferable to chimney draught.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design furnaces and flues to optimize combustion stoichiometry and heat transfer; consider mechanical draught systems to reduce waste up the chimney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use better materials and workmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt better materials (e.g., mild steels instead of crude iron) and more careful workmanship, especially in boilers, and improve proportions and forms of details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in higher-quality materials and precision manufacturing—improvements in tools and skilled design enable gains in efficiency and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational management matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Care, skill, and intelligence in management are essential to economical operation and safety; 'the best is the cheapest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize training, skilled operators, and attentive management practices as part of overall efficiency strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce heat remaining at exhaust
rubrics_metrics.description: A very large portion of heat loss is due to heat remaining in the steam at exhaust; reduce the quantity of heat at the opening of the exhaust-valve and retain/rework it if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use strategies like dry steam, steam-jackets, high engine-speed, low-conductivity cylinder linings, compound expansion, and heat-recovery methods to minimize exhaust heat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate and remove mechanical/physical obstructions
rubrics_metrics.description: If advancement is checked by inadequate returns, the engineer must detect the cause (purely physical/mechanical obstructions) and find ways to remove them where not physically impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach setbacks diagnostically: analyze losses, failure modes, and manufacturing limitations; innovate to remove the root cause rather than abandon promising directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Piston speed limits imply design trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Increasing piston-speed approaches limits where certain valve-gears cannot function; designers must adapt valve-gear forms and governor designs to meet high-speed requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When targeting higher speeds, plan valve-gear and control systems accordingly; avoid relying on mechanisms that cannot keep up with mechanical timing constraints.
